home.title: AI Ethics Suitcase
home.subtitle: My dog ate my students' exams!

intro.headerTitle: Welcome to the AI Ethics Suitcase!

tour.0: Welcome to the AI Ethics Suitcase! Mr. Turner needs to grade his students' exams, but his dog tore up the answer sheets! He can only read a few exams now. So he needs to decide in some other way who passed. You may skip this explanation if you already know charts.
tour.1: The teacher remembers that he asked the parents to keep track of how his students spent their time before the exam. He will write it down in this chart.
tour.2: This is the X-axis, where he writes down the study time in minutes.
tour.3: This is the Y-axis, where he writes down the leisure time in minutes.
tour.4: The teacher also decides on these symbols for passing and failing students, so he can look again if he gets confused.
tour.5: For example, this circle shows a student who passed. The student studied 150 minutes and had 300 minutes of leisure time.
tour.6: This square is for a student who failed. The student studied 100 minutes and had 200 minutes of leisure time.
tour.7: The tutorial has three levels. Once you are done with a level, press this button to go to the next one. The teacher already has an idea for how to grade the students.

alerts.invalidBounds: Please start and end your drawing outside the graph area.
alerts.invalidIntersections: The curve must start and end outside the graph in the striped area. Please try again.

stages.0: [1/3] The teacher starts with an example of 4 students. His plan is to classify Pass and Fail students using a straight line. Drag or click in the chart to draw a line to separate the passing and failing students.
stages.1: [1/3] Now click to make a second point for the line.
stages.3: [2/3] This line is called a 'linear classifier' (linear comes from line, to classify means to group). Change your line by dragging the black circles or drawing a new line. When done, press 'Next' to continue.
stages.4: [3/3] Complete! You can now see which students your line classified correctly and incorrectly. In the next level we will learn how to grade a classifier.

instructions.1: [1/5] Click inside the pass area to add a student who has passed.
instructions.2: [2/5] Now click inside the fail area to add a student who has failed.
instructions.3: [3/5] What happens when you place a student who has failed in the pass area?
instructions.4: [4/5] Finally, place a student who has passed in the fail area.
instructions.5: [5/5] Great! You have classified all types of students. Press 'End Tutorial' to continue.

level1.goal: How do you grade a classifier?

tour.0: The teacher looks at what happens for some of his students. Luckily, he has some exams that he has already graded and can still read. He will need a way to see how well the linear classifier works for these students.
tour.1: He draws this linear classifier, splitting the chart into 2 parts. The left area has the students who Fail and the right area has those who Pass.
tour.2: This student passed, and the classifier put them in the Pass group. This is right! This is a 'True Positive'.
tour.3: This student failed, and the classifier put them in the Fail group. This is right! This is a 'True Negative'.
tour.4: This student failed, but the classifier put them in the Pass group. This is wrong! This is a 'False Positive'.
tour.5: The student passed, but the classifier put them in the Fail group. This is wrong! This is a 'False Negative'.
tour.6: The results show the number of true positives, true negatives, false positives, and false negatives. The 'accuracy' tells you how good the classifier is: count the students it got right, and divide that by the total number of students.

stages.0: [1/4] The teacher decides to practice drawing classifiers based on old exam data. Drag or click to draw the classifier line to separate the pass from the fail area.
stages.1: [1/4] Now click the second point to draw the classifier line.
stages.3: [2/4] Adjust your classifier by dragging the black circles or drawing a new line. When happy with it, click 'Next' to continue.
stages.4: [3/4] Complete! You can now see the classifier results. Ms. Swinton, the computer science teacher, sees Mr. Turner practicing. She suggests using AI to find the line with the best performance! You can now compare your classifier with the best classifier found by AI.
stages.5: [4/4] Compare your classifier with the best classifier. You can see both results next to each other.

stages.0: [1/4] The teacher tries harder with more data from past exams! Drag or click to draw the classifier line to separate the pass from the fail area.
stages.1: [1/4] Now click the second point to draw the classifier line.
stages.3: [2/4] Adjust your classifier by dragging the black circles or drawing a new line. When happy with it, click 'Next' to continue.
stages.4: [3/4] Complete! You can now see the results. You can compare your classifier with the best classifier found by AI.
stages.5: [4/4] Compare your classifier with the best classifier. You can see both results next to each other.

stages.0: [1/4] The teacher wants to try separating the students using a curve instead of a line. Draw a curve starting and ending outside the graph area (within the striped zone).
stages.1: [1/4] The teacher wants to try separating the students using a curve. Draw a curve starting and ending outside the graph area (within the striped zone).
stages.2: [2/4] You may create a new classifier by drawing again. When happy with it, click 'Next' to continue.
stages.3: [3/4] Complete! You can now see the results. The curve is so much better than a line! The teacher is excited. Maybe he never has to grade again! He takes more exams to test his curve.
stages.4: [4/4] Now switch between seen and unseen data (the newly grabbed exams). Notice how performance may be different on new data! The teacher sighs and gets back to reading his students' work.

tutorialDialog.title: Welcome to the Overfitting level!
tutorialDialog.message: So far, the teacher has only tried linear classifiers. He wonders what happens if he uses a more complex shape than a straight line. In this level, you can try a curve instead of a line. After that, you can check how the classifier performs on students it has never seen before.

levelfreeplay.goal: Try to beat the best classifier within a time limit!

stages.0: [1/3] Drag or click to draw the classifier line to separate the pass from the fail area.
stages.1: [1/3] Now click the second point to draw the classifier line.
stages.3: [2/3] Adjust your classifier by dragging the black circles or drawing a new line. When happy with it, press 'Finish'.
stages.6: [3/3] Complete! You can now compare your classifier with the best classifier, and switch between the seen and unseen data.

tutorialDialog.title: Welcome to the Free Play level!
tutorialDialog.message: In this level, you should draw the classifier as quickly as you can. Try to beat the solution found by AI! You can also compare performance on seen and unseen data. Watch the timer, and have fun exploring!

finish.title: Congratulations!
finish.moral: Unfortunately for Mr. Turner, even Ms. Swinton's best classifier makes mistakes. He realizes this method of grading is not fair to the students. Mr. Turner is sad that his idea did not work. He takes a roll of sticky tape and slowly puts the torn exams back together. Also, he promises to bring a box of chocolates to the next class because the students had to wait so long for their results.
